summary: Iteration 2: Tested new admin auth flow (backend + frontend), updated landing content, mobile hamburger, and join-form regression. Backend 16/17 pytest passed. Frontend admin login/dashboard/logout, filter chips, contacts table, mobile menu, landing content (hero launch badge, programs flagship cards, Konsil Penasehat Kehormatan incl. Sandiaga Uno, footer 'Salam Otak Sehat, Indonesia Cerdas', EN toggle), join form + admin visibility — all pass. Two issues found: (1) brute-force lockout doesn't trigger because identifier uses request.client.host which varies across load-balanced backend replicas (429 never returned); (2) Indonesian ecosystem block is missing the `cooperation` array so the 'Lima Pilar Kerja Sama' chips (data-testid=cooperation-pillars) do NOT render in ID (default) language — only in EN.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout (429 after 5 fails) never triggers. RCA: identifier is `{request.client.host}:{email}` but the app runs behind Kubernetes ingress with multiple replicas — different backend pods see different peer IPs (observed 10.208.128.9 and 10.208.128.10 in login_attempts collection), so counts split across identifiers and never reach 5. Fix: derive client IP from X-Forwarded-For header (first hop) or key lockout on email only.

integration_issues.issue: `cooperation-pillars` div is not rendered on the default Indonesian view because i18n.js `content.id.ecosystem` has no `cooperation` array (only `content.en.ecosystem.cooperation` exists). Users in ID never see the 'Lima Pilar Kerja Sama' chips.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout identifier: use X-Forwarded-For (or email-only) so counts don't split across replicas.

Add `cooperation: ['Edukasi','Aktivasi','Advokasi','Kolaborasi','Riset']` (or the doc-approved wording) plus `coopLabel: 'Lima Pilar Kerja Sama'` to `content.id.ecosystem` in /app/frontend/src/i18n.js so the chips render in Indonesian.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: brute-force key uses request.client.host — unreliable behind ingress; also allows an attacker on a rotating IP to bypass lockout entirely.
server.py: set_cookie uses secure=True which is fine for the HTTPS preview but will silently drop cookies on http://localhost during dev; consider deriving `secure` from env or request scheme.
AdminDashboard.js: on any error in the /auth/me or /admin/contacts call the user is silently redirected to /admin/login — no toast/error surfaced (a 500 would feel like a logout).
server.py stores contacts.created_at as ISO string then re-parses on read — inconsistent with the ContactSubmission model (datetime); would be cleaner to persist as native datetime.
CORS still `allow_origins='*'` with `allow_credentials=True` — browsers reject credentials with wildcard; harmless right now (frontend sends Bearer + same-origin cookie) but should be tightened.
seed_data_creation: Created a few TEST_ contact submissions via API + one via UI (TEST_PlaywrightUser). Also polluted login_attempts collection with lockout-solo@example.com and lockout-test@example.com entries.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin auth wiring works end-to-end (Bearer token + httpOnly cookie both accepted). Lockout logic bug requires X-Forwarded-For based key. Programs, Governance/Advisory Council, launch badge, footer tagline, mobile hamburger and 1024x768/390x844 responsive all verified. Only the ID-language cooperation-pillars chips are missing.
rca of the issue: Lockout: MongoDB login_attempts collection shows the same failed email split into two identifiers e.g. '10.208.128.9:lockout-solo@example.com' (count=3) and '10.208.128.10:lockout-solo@example.com' (count=4). Kubernetes ingress balances requests to 2 backend pods, each recording request.client.host from its own peer, so the 5-attempt threshold is never reached from a single client. Fix should key lockout on email (optionally combined with the true client IP from X-Forwarded-For).
